source.title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications

accepted.question_text: Let T:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] be an Archimedean t-norm, and let its associated negation be N_T(x)=sup{t in [0,1] : T(x,t)=0}. Assume N_T is involutive, meaning N_T(N_T(x))=x for every x in [0,1]. Must such a t-norm T be conditionally cancellative or left-continuous, or can there exist an Archimedean t-norm with involutive associated negation that fails both of those properties?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 (B. Jayaram). Does there exist any Archimedean t-norm T , whose NT is involutive but is not conditionally cancellative or left-continuous? In other words, is an Archimedean t-norm T whose NT is involutive necessarily conditionally cancellative or left-continuous?

accepted.question_text: Within a chosen class of fuzzy implications on [0,1]^2, such as (S,N)-implications, R-implications, f-implications, or g-implications, characterize exactly those implications I for which the exchange principle I(x, I(y, z)) = I(y, I(x, z)) is preserved under the lattice operations of pointwise minimum and pointwise maximum. Equivalently, determine which subfamilies remain closed under forming I \/ J and I /\ J while still satisfying the exchange principle.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 (M. Baczynski, B. Jayaram). Characterize the subfamily of all fuzzy implications ((S,N)-implications, R-implications, etc.) which preserve the (EP) for lattice operations.

accepted.question_text: Let n >= 2 and let C:[0,1]^n -> [0,1] be an n-ary copula, meaning that C is n-increasing and satisfies the usual copula boundary conditions. Define C_1 by C_1(x_1,...,x_n)=C(x_1,...,x_n)-product_{i=1}^n (x_i-C(x_1,...,x_n)). Is C_1 always n-increasing, and hence itself an n-ary copula? If not, characterize those n-ary copulas C for which C_1 is again an n-ary copula.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (Mesiar). Let C : [0, 1]^n -> [0, 1] be an n-ary copula. Define C1 : [0, 1]^n -> [0, 1] by C1(x1,...,xn) = C(x1,...,xn) - product_{i=1}^n (xi - C(x1,...,xn)). Is the function C1 n-increasing, i.e., is it an n-copula? If in general not, characterize all n-copulas C such that C1 is an n-copula, too.

accepted.question_text: Let C:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] be a 2-copula and let its dual copula be C*(x,y)=x+y-C(x,y). For a parameter lambda in [0,1], define C^(lambda) by C^(lambda)(x,y)=C(x,y)/(1+lambda-lambda C*(x,y)). Is C^(lambda) always a 2-copula? If not, characterize, for a given 2-copula C, the set of parameters lambda in [0,1] for which C^(lambda) is a 2-copula.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 (Mesiar). Let C : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] be a 2-copula. For lambda in [0, 1], define C^(lambda) : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] by C^(lambda) = C/(1 + lambda - lambda C*). Is the function C^(lambda) a 2-copula, too? If not, in general, characterize the set of all parameters lambda in [0, 1] for which C^(lambda) is a 2-copula.

accepted.question_text: Let U be a uninorm on [0,1] with neutral element e in (0,1), and define the induced relation x <=_U y to mean that there exists z in [0,1] such that U(z,y)=x. Suppose U does not contain any zoomed-out representable uninorm in the sense defined in the source. Is that condition sufficient to ensure that the induced relation <=_U is antisymmetric?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 (M. Kalina). Is the condition that U does not contain a zoomed-out representable uninorm sufficient for the relation <=_U to be anti-symmetric?

accepted.question_text: Define a satisfactory notion of penalty functions and penalty-based functions on the lattice L([0,1]) of closed subintervals of [0,1], in a way that still recovers averaging aggregation operators on that lattice as penalty-based functions. The definition should handle the order structure of L([0,1]), including the partial order [a,b] <=_L [c,d] iff a<=c and b<=d, and possibly also linear admissible orders extending that partial order.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 (H. Bustince, J. Fernandez, M. Pagola, D. Paternain, E. Barrenechea). To define properly penalty functions and penalty-based functions in the lattice of closed subintervals of the unit interval [0, 1], L([0, 1]), in such a way that averaging aggregation operators in this lattice can be recovered as penalty-based functions.

accepted.question_text: Let K:R -> [0,1] be a normal generating function for generalized uniform fuzzy partitions of the real line, and assume K satisfies the symmetry condition integral from 1/2-y to y+1/2 of K(x) dx = y for every y in [0,1/2]. For positive real numbers h and r and any central node x_0, consider the scaled generating function (r/h)K used in the quadruple ((r/h)K, h, r, x_0). Is it true that this quadruple determines a generalized uniform fuzzy partition if and only if h/r is a natural number? If not, identify a replacement condition of comparable simplicity under which such an iff criterion holds.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 (M. Holcapek, I. Perfilieva, V. Novak and V. Kreinovich). Let K be a normal generating function satisfying the symmetry condition (5). Then, (K_{r/h}, h, r, x0) determines a GUFP iff h/r in N.

accepted.question_text: In quantitative logic, a formula is assigned a meta-degree by aggregating its truth degrees over all evaluations of its propositional variables, using either a normalized weighted sum on a finite truth-degree set or an integral on [0,1]. Which other kinds of aggregation operators are suitable for defining these meta-degrees, and how should the choice of aggregation operator depend on the intended applications of the logic?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1 (S. Gottwald). Which other types of aggregation operators instead of the integral or the weighted sum are suitable here? And how depends their choice from intended applications?

accepted.question_text: In the quantitative-logic framework where meta-degrees are obtained by aggregating formula truth degrees across valuations, is a measure on the truth-degree set genuinely necessary, as it is in the integral-based case, or can a satisfactory theory be developed without introducing a measure?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2 (S. Gottwald). Particularly, does one need – as in the case of the integral – a measure in the truth degree set, or can one do well without, too?

accepted.question_text: Generalize the quantitative-logic setup from the case where the truth-degree set is the real unit interval or a finite subset of it to the case where the truth-degree set is an arbitrary lattice. In particular, determine how formulas, truth functions, and meta-degree assignments should be formulated in that lattice-valued setting.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3 (S. Gottwald). How to generalize this setting for the case that the truth degree set is a lattice?

accepted.question_text: When the truth-degree set in quantitative logic is a lattice rather than [0,1], determine what the appropriate notions of measures on lattices and aggregation operators on lattices should be so that the meta-degree machinery of quantitative logic remains meaningful and useful.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.4 (S. Gottwald). Particularly, what about suitable measures on lattices; and what about aggregation operators on lattices?

accepted.question_text: A semicopula is a nondecreasing map S:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] with neutral element 1 and S(x,y)<=min(x,y). Characterize all semicopulas S for which the subadditivity-type inequality S(x+y,z) <= S(x,z) + S(y,z) holds whenever x,y,z are in [0,1] and x+y is still in [0,1].

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1 (O. Hutnik). To characterize all the semicopulas S for which the inequality S(x + y, z) <= S(x, z) + S(y, z) holds for each x, y in [0, 1] such that x + y in [0, 1].

accepted.question_text: For the smallest semicopula-based universal integral I_S(m,f)=sup_{t in [0,1]} S(t,h_{m,f}(t)), where h_{m,f}(t)=m({x in X : f(x)>=t}), characterize those semicopulas S for which the translation identity I_S(m,f+alpha)=I_S(m,f)+alpha holds for every measurable space (X,A), every capacity m on A, every measurable f:X->[0,1], and every alpha in [0,1] with f+alpha still taking values in [0,1].

evidence.quote: Problem 9.2 (O. Hutnik). Characterize a class of semicopulas S, for which the equality IS(m, f + alpha) = IS(m, f) + alpha holds for each (X,A) in S, each (m, f) in M(X,A) x F(X,A) and alpha in [0, 1] such that f + alpha in [0, 1].

accepted.question_text: For the smallest semicopula-based universal integral I_S, characterize those semicopulas S for which, for every alpha in [0,1], every measurable space (X,A), every capacity m on A, and every measurable f:X->[0,1], one has I_S(m, S(alpha,f)) = S(alpha, I_S(m,f)).

evidence.quote: Problem 9.3 (O. Hutnik). To characterize a class of semicopulas S for which the property (forall alpha in [0, 1]) IS(m, S(alpha, f)) = S(alpha,IS(m, f)) holds for all (X,A) in S and all (m, f) in M(X,A) x F(X,A).

accepted.question_text: Characterize all non-additive set functions m for which, on every measurable space, strict convergence in measure with respect to m is equivalent to ordinary convergence in measure with respect to m.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.4 (O. Hutnik). Characterize all the non-additive set functions for which strict convergence in measure is equivalent to convergence in measure on any measurable space.

accepted.question_text: Determine for which classes of semicopulas S, and possibly for which classes of capacities, strict convergence in measure is equivalent to convergence in mean defined by the smallest semicopula-based universal integral I_S.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.5 (O. Hutnik). For which class of semicopulas (of capacities, eventually) is strict convergence in measure equivalent to mean convergence?

accepted.question_text: Let E be an orthocomplete homogeneous effect algebra, and let S(E) denote its set of sharp elements. Assume S(E) is a lattice. Must E itself then be a lattice effect algebra, or can one construct a counterexample under these hypotheses?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.1 (G. Jenca). Prove or disprove: if E is an orthocomplete homogeneous effect algebra E such that S(E) is a lattice, then E is a lattice effect algebra.

accepted.question_text: Find a generator for the variety SMV of state MV-algebras. In particular, determine whether such a generator is connected in a natural way with the MV-algebra of the real interval [0,1], analogous to how the state-morphism MV-algebra ([0,1]^2, tau_[0,1]) generates the variety of state morphism MV-algebras.

evidence.quote: Problem 11.1 (A. Dvurecenskij). According to [11, Theorem 5.4 (3)], find a generator of the variety of state MV-algebras. Is this generator connected in some way with the MV-algebra of the real interval?
